subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should cron post-run verification be implemented as a scheduler-owned bounded verifier contract, a fail-capable plugin hook, or deferred until a broader agent outcome-verification API exists?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution adds public cron config/protocol/state, retry behavior, and unattended command execution semantics that require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
options.body: Define typed post-run verification owned by cron, with command or plugin adapters, timeout and output caps, redaction, persisted status, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

options.title: Add plugin seam first
options.body: Expose a fail-capable cron post-run hook that can return pass, fail, retry, or escalation decisions while keeping verifier implementation outside core.

options.title: Defer verifier API
options.body: Keep this issue as the specific design tracker until maintainers settle a broader outcome-verification architecture across cron and outbound hooks.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
recommendation.body: Define typed post-run verification owned by cron, with command or plugin adapters, timeout and output caps, redaction, persisted status, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and has the strongest recent history on the cron schema/runtime/doc surfaces.
